Difference Between Analog and Digital Instruments at a Glance

The difference between analog and digital instruments is in how the reading is presented. An analog instrument shows the measured value as a continuous pointer position on a scale, while a digital instrument converts the signal with an ADC and shows it as discrete numbers on a display.

ParameterAnalog instrumentDigital instrument
Output formContinuous pointer deflectionNumeric display in discrete steps
Signal processingMechanical or simple electricalADC, microprocessor and software
AccuracyLower, affected by friction and wearHigher, with fine resolution
Reading errorsParallax and interpolation errorsNo parallax error
Power needMany work without external powerNeeds supply or battery
Data storageNot possibleMemory, logging and trending
CommunicationUsually none, or 4 to 20 mAHART, Modbus, Profibus
Trend visibilityEasy to see a rising or falling valueNeeds a bar graph or trend screen
ExamplesBourdon pressure gauge, PMMC voltmeterDigital multimeter, smart transmitter

Choose an analog gauge where a simple local indication is enough, and a digital instrument where accuracy, recording and integration with a PLC or DCS are needed.
